central_claim.note: Structural and demographic organization, not risky behaviors: the abstract's own wording.

evidence.note: Cross-sectional network data, three reservation schools (E1); N = 247 from the abstract without naming the stage (E2 part); ERGMs named (E3 part).
Up to 10 directed nominations, Network Canvas (E4); only the AI identity measure of E5.
AMEs comparable across schools (implies per-school models); the robustness models with structural terms and substance use are described as a method, without their result, so no F7.

key_findings.note: No consistent sender, receiver or homophily effects; isolated effects did not replicate (paper's wording). Exceptions not named, as in the calibrated F1 matches.
The contrast with non-AI populations is the paper's, for depression.
Incoming ties centralized only in School C (F5 half, no outdegree); substance homophily only in School B is a detail of F1. Context-dependence follows the paper's 'suggest' (p.16).

scope_and_limits.note: Selection versus influence and association versus cause (L3); one developmental period at one time point (L4, credited when the developmental stage is mentioned).
Bias such as false consensus; not that it could inflate similarity among friends.

flags.text: The note says the authors 'revise' the generalizations of peer-network research; the paper says it 'moves beyond generalizations' and tests whether one finding generalizes (T3 dropped 'revises').

theoretical_positioning.note: Testing half of T3, without what is replicated and what is disputed.
Endogenous mechanisms shaped by community norms (T2); 'universal but calibrated by context' is the paper's p.14 wording. Same call as calibration.

interlocutor_claim.note: Receiver and homophily both given, with the dispute; refs 13 (Ali), 11 (Schaefer, Haas, Bishop), 22 (Haas and Schaefer) correctly attributed.
